Definition: a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare G977, G1016); to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze:--feed, keep.
BiblicalUsage: To feed is the word for pasturing, tending a flock — and it appears nine times. In Matthew 8:30 a herd of swine was feeding on the mountain when the demons begged to enter them. In Luke 15:15 the prodigal joins himself to a citizen who sends him into the fields to feed swine. In John 21:15 Jesus says, feed my lambs, and in John 21:17 he says it again, feed my sheep.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the feeding in John is the whole charge of the ministry: the risen Lord does not ask Peter for a plan, he asks him to feed the sheep.
